messages.author: 701dadf5d5bd3f3b
messages.subject: Re: MS1 Label Free Dataset
parts:
Dear Lorenzo,

the error message means that in the input file the number of rows for some features (i.e. combinations of protein ids and peptide ion ids) exceeds the number of runs. In other words, some combinations of protein and peptide ids appear multiple times in a same file. The error message lists the peptides and the runs where this is the case. You need to check the input file, and make sure that the naming is correct.

Best wishes
Olga

Dear Olga,

Thanks for your prompt response. Based on your response, I checked a the MS Stats Input Report of my simple case (just one protein with version of the same canonical peptides with and without phosphorylation) and found an issue. The report template was exporting the PeptideSequence and therefore the phosphorylated peptides and the normal peptides were indistinguishable. I did a quick fix modifying your Template and replaced PeptideSequence by PeptideModifiedSequence and MSStats Group Comparison was able to finish. So I decided to load my big report and try with the new template for MS Stats Input Report and I got the same error. Again looking closely I found the issue, it seems to me that your package cannot handle situations in which the same Peptide Modified Sequence is not unique and present in more than one protein. Am I correct? Do you have a fix for it?

Best regards,

Lorenzp

messages.author: 701dadf5d5bd3f3b
messages.subject: Re: MS1 Label Free Dataset
parts:
Dear Lorenzo,

I am glad that you could make progress. Regarding shared ions: currently we do require that a (modified) peptide sequence is uniquely mapped to a protein. If an ion belongs to multiple proteins than its abundance has contributions from multiple sources, and it will negatively affect individual protein-level quantifications. In theory it is possible to view the abundance of shared ions as a mixture and deconvolute it computationally, but we don't implement this yet. In practice we suggest to either exclude these ions from protein-level analysis, or work with peptide-level quantification as opposed to protein-level quantification. If you are interested in PTMs, peptide-level quantification may be more appropriate. (In this case, just use peptide names in the protein name column).

I hope that this helps at least somewhat
Sincerely
Olga

messages.author: 7cec1ca129682d1f
messages.subject: Re: MS1 Label Free Dataset
parts:
Olga and Lorenzo,

I found this thread after running into the same problem with my label-free MS1 dataset and think I've found a work-around. I'm performing the MS1 analysis in Skyline, exporting the results, and running MSstats.daily 2.1.6 in R.

I was able to narrow down this error to two problems with the imported dataset:
  1. If there are duplicate peptides in the document (i.e. between protein isoforms), MSstats flags the peptides as duplicates. To get rid of duplicates, I used the "remove repeated peptides" feature in Skyline (Edit-->Refine-->Remove repeated peptides). This option will remove all repeated peptides except for the first occurrence.
  2. If a peptide has multiple charge states (i.e. +2 and +3), MSstats flags the peptide as a duplicate. Lorenzo, it looks this is your problem. There are +2 and +3 peptides in your document (I copied one example below). Instead of changing "PrecursorCharge" and "ProductCharge" columns to "NA" like the MSstats manual suggests, I kept the charges in the document.
Peptide with multiple charges:

CNAVGEVKDYEPPFGSK_2_precursor [M+1]_2, CNAVGEVKDYEPPFGSK_2_precursor [M+2]_2, CNAVGEVKDYEPPFGSK_2_precursor_2, CNAVGEVKDYEPPFGSK_3_precursor [M+1]_3, CNAVGEVKDYEPPFGSK_3_precursor [M+2]_3, CNAVGEVKDYEPPFGSK_3_precursor_3

Olga, assuming a peptide is unique, how will multiply-charged peptides affect protein level quantification?

Scott

messages.author: 701dadf5d5bd3f3b
messages.subject: Re: MS1 Label Free Dataset
parts:
Dear Scott,

Thank you for your post, this is indeed the right solution. MSstats treats all peptide ions as different features. I.e., a peptide with charge +2 and a same peptide with charge +3 will be considered different features. We do not distinguish the nature of the features (different peptides sequences or different charges).

HTH
Sincerely
Olga

Sorry for not answering sooner. Both Meena and I have difficulties interpreting your question. What software do you use to locate and quantify the peaks? Are you talking about quantifying a feature from several peaks in the isotopic distribution? Could you please provide more details, we will do our best to help.

If your question relates to the isotopic distribution, then the important thing is to make the same decision consistently across all the runs. E.g., if a feature is quantified from the most intense peak, then it should be done in every run. Take the sum of intensities of all the peaks in the isotopic distribution is dangerous in presence of missing values.

I  am not sure if I answered your question. Please give us more details, or maybe an example, if this is not the case.

We are using Skyline to quantify peaks. Normally, it adds together the peak area from the monoisotopic and M+1 peaks to get a more robust measure of peptide intensity. The "MSstats export" file reports two separate peaks instead. So it outputs e.g.:

PeptideSequence  Charge   FragmentIon     ...   Intensity 
SSESKPEFFYSEEQR  2        precursor             2523043
SSESKPEFFYSEEQR  2        precursor [M+1]       3896546

For each peptide in the results. As Skyline was doing this automatically, my interpretation was that this is the desired behavior--that using both peaks separately allowed for a better model. Is this not a good idea?

In any case, the latest version of MSstats rejects this input because the PeptideSequence is the same--even though the FragmentIon column differs, it does not consider them separate features. It looked like Scott Goulding (and maybe Lorenzo Vega) was having the same issue, as I can see that they have multiple isotopic peaks with the same sequence/charge, and MSstats is rejecting them.

Like I said earlier, an older version of MSstats (2.1.3 or 2.2.0, installed via BioConductor) doesn't have an issue with this, so I was wondering if it was a new bug, or an old bug, or a deliberate change in behavior.

thanks for your help,
- James

messages.author: 701dadf5d5bd3f3b
messages.subject: Re: MS1 Label Free Dataset
parts:
Dear James,

Sorry for not answering sooner. Part of the reason for the silence is that we don't have a fully informed solution. The previous version of MSstats worked 'by accident' (i.e., we didn't do an extensive checking for such features, and therefore they were treated as if they were additional independent replicates - which is not quite the right thing to do).

For the time being, my advice is to use your best judgement. The important thing is to make sure that the same feature is consistently profiled in all runs, and the choice is independent from the intensity. (E.g., if you use the monoisotopic peak, use it consistently across runs. If you take the sum, take the sum of the same number of peaks across runs. Selecting the most intense peak in each run is incorrect, as it will bias the quantification). If you decide to separately use multiple such features, you will need to edit the dataset, e.g. add a character to the peptide sequence to provide a unique name.

We will also actively look into this on our side, and are hoping to provide a more informed and data-benchmarked solution in a longer term.

I hope that this helps at least somewhat
Sincerely
Olga
